title: David and Peter prove regenerate can fall—and remain death-liable while impenitent
source_text: XIV. Quam Thesin sic in sequentibus confirmant: Exemplis Davidis ac Petri constat posse renatos in gravissima peccata seipsos praecipitare, Deo ita quandoque permittente, ut discant cum humilitate agnoscere, non suis viribus aut meritis, sed solius Dei misericordia se fuisse a morte aeterna servatos, & vita aeterna donatos. Dum hujusmodi peccatis inhaerent, iisque secure acquiescunt, indignatio Dei paterna contra eos laborat. Si justitias meas profanaverint, & mandata mea non custodierint, visitabo in virga iniquitates eorum, & in verberibus peccata eorum. Tribulatio & angustia in omnem animam hominis operantis malum. Quin etiam reatum damnabilem contrahunt, ita ut dum in eo statu impoenitentes persistunt, nec debeant, nec possint aliter sibi persuadere, quam se esse morti obnoxios. Si secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini. Sunt enim capitali crimine constricti, cujus merito, secundum divinam ordinationem morti subjacent, quamvis nondum morti traditi sint, neque si paternam Dei amorem spectemus, tradendi, sed ab hoc peccato prius eripiendi, ut sic ex mortis reatu eripiantur. Denique, pro praesenti conditione, amittunt aptitudinem ad ingrediendum regnum coelorum; quia in illud regnum non intrabit aliquid coinquinatum, aut abominationem faciens. Coelestis enim corona non imponitur nisi iis, Qui bonum certamen certarunt, & cursum suum in fide & sanctitate consummarunt. Ineptus ergo ad hanc coronam adipiscendam quisquis impietatis operibus adhuc adhaerescit. Psalm. 89. 31. Rom. 2. 9. & 8. 13. Apoc. 21. 27. 2 Tim. 4. 8.
pass_a_gloss: Which Thesis they thus confirm in what follows: By the examples of David and Peter it is established that the regenerate can cast themselves headlong into most grievous sins, God so sometimes permitting, that they may learn with humility to acknowledge that they were saved from eternal death and gifted with eternal life not by their own powers or merits but by the mercy of God alone. While they cling to such sins and securely rest in them, the paternal indignation of God works against them. If they shall have profaned my righteousnesses and shall not have kept my commandments, I will visit their iniquities with a rod and their sins with stripes. Tribulation and anguish upon every soul of man that does evil. Nay they also contract damnable guilt, so that while they persist impenitent in that state they neither ought nor can persuade themselves otherwise than that they are liable to death. If you live according to the flesh, you shall die. For they are bound with a capital crime, by whose desert, according to the divine ordination, they are subject to death, although they have not yet been delivered to death, nor, if we look to the paternal love of God, are they to be delivered, but are first to be snatched from this sin, that so they may be snatched from the guilt of death. Finally, for their present condition, they lose the fitness for entering the kingdom of heaven; because into that kingdom nothing defiled shall enter, or that works abomination. For the heavenly crown is imposed only on those who have fought the good fight and finished their course in faith and holiness. Unfit therefore for obtaining this crown is whoever still clings to works of impiety. Psalm 89:31. Rom. 2:9 and 8:13. Rev. 21:27. 2 Tim. 4:8.
pass_b_english: David and Peter show regenerate saints can plunge into grievous sin under God’s permission for humility.
While they rest impenitent they owe damnable guilt, lose present fitness for heaven, and must not pretend safety.

choices.why: Dangerous false peace in unrepented grave sin.
